3: ⦅The purpose of this section is to explain why a trust-oriented authorisation framework is required and to introduce its dimensions. It should be noted at the outset that, in addition to the four foundational dimensions RO1 to RO4 that are introduced below, the proposed framework has been extended to incorporate temporal validity and lifecycle trust (RO5), which was originally planned for the next stage.⦆⦅⦆ In particular, validity periods and expiration are enforced at the point of evaluation and mirrored on-chain, revocation is executed as a verifiable blockchain transaction, and consent progresses through controlled state transitions. This is important because trust cannot be regarded as permanently established at the moment a consent is created.
4: ⦅Adversarial and negative testing has been undertaken using the HALAH prototype, which is the Patient Consent Management Platform for History Access by Authorised Healthcare Providers described in Section 6.8. This testing covers per-dimension denial scenarios, guardian signature-rejection tests and tests of tampered and expired zero-knowledge proofs. It also includes a live negative evaluation on the Ethereum Sepolia testnet. Formal security analysis has not yet been undertaken and remains the subject of the next research stage.⦆

⦅RO5 has moved from planned work to implemented capability. The consent validity interval [t~s~, t~e~] is now enforced by the temporal predicate V~T~ at every access request. The interval is additionally stored on-chain in the SBT as the notBefore and expiry fields, so that temporal validity can be verified independently of the application. The consent lifecycle is implemented as an explicit state machine comprising the states PENDING_SIGNATURE, PENDING_TOKEN, NOT_STARTED, ACTIVE, EXPIRED and REVOKED. Revocation is enforced end-to-end. The patient's withdrawal updates the application state and is confirmed as a revoke transaction on Sepolia in block 11,771,307. After that point the contract itself reports the token as invalid and subsequent access requests are denied. What remains for the next stage is therefore the dynamic and delegated dimension of lifecycle trust, such as consent modification, delegation and guardian-set changes, rather than temporal enforcement itself. ⦅The temporal predicate enforced at every access request is, as defined in Eq.
